edit.find: These distances are static estimates (8 px x frames); they were not measured at runtime.
edit.with: Measured: the lock lasts the full 64 (type 1) or 32 (type 3) frames, the peak rise is 204 and 50 pixels, the end height is the launch height (type 1) or 8 pixels lower (type 3), and playerSpeedEw is +/-7 or +/-8 in the first frame after the lock is released.

edit.find: i.e. one full animation cycle of Y movement at -8 (north, animation $1E, chain $10) or +8 (south, animation $19, chain $0F) per frame.
edit.with: i.e. one full animation cycle of Y movement at -8 (north, animation $1E, chain $10) or +8 (south, animation $19, chain $0F) per frame. Measured: a north cycle is 8 moving frames plus 1 hold frame (64 px per loop), a south cycle 4 moving frames plus 1 hold frame (32 px per loop). A type 9 north ramp (4 loops) and a type $11 south ramp (8 loops) both move the player 256 px, a type 3 north ramp 64 px. The east/west climbs show animation $24 (ramp_west, east-bound) and $21 (ramp_east, west-bound) for the whole arc.

edit.find: Whether the player's step size always hits it was not checked at runtime.
edit.with: The equality is not guaranteed: the player has to stop exactly on the ramp coordinate. Ramps backed by a wall launch because the wall stops the player on the coordinate (191 of 192 forced-speed approaches to the Great Wall ramps launched, and the Itory ramp_east launched on a natural approach). On open ground only 3 of 16 approaches launched (the arrival step has to divide the distance), and ramp_south in scene A1 launched in 5 of 16 approaches (0 of 8 at speed 6). A player left 1-15 px short stays in stage 2 and the ramp waits every frame; 16 px or more disarms it. Walking and running on flat ground (speed 2 and 3) never arm a ramp; the natural approach measured (Itory ramp_east) arms at speed -7 on the slope band, and an approach whose speed falls below 6 before it enters the window does not arm.

edit.find: UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME: whether another path adds speed on these ramps, and whether a +/-1 step per approach is the intended feel, was not checked.
edit.with: Measured: the booster writes only playerSpeedEw (no write to playerSpeedNs from the booster in any case traced). It boosts once per approach: a run west at -3 becomes -4 at 32 px and stays -4 for 16 frames while the player is inside the 48-px box, and the next boost comes only after the player has been more than 48 px away. With only the NS speed nonzero, playerSpeedEw becomes +1 for one frame and is 0 again in the next. Walking on flat ground never opens the gate (both speed words are 0 when it runs); in the one walk case that opened it, the player was walking up a slope and the slope code had written the speed word.

edit.find: There is no animation during the glide; the slide's looping frame stays on screen.
edit.with: There is no animation during the glide; the slide's looping frame stays on screen. Measured on a south trigger ($0E = 7) and a north trigger ($0E = 8): the player moves 112 px south in 28 frames or 128 px north in 32 frames, then the finish animation runs 16 frames (44 and 48 locked frames in total) and the player stands on a free row 7 or 8 tiles from the trigger, past a wall band of two solid rows with open and half-solid rows between them. The player's Y reaches the trigger row because the wall directly below that row stops the slide there, and a slide that has already ended (animation back to idle) fails the sprite-bank check and does not fire.
